equations.title: 4,000-Experiment Scaling Law on 512 H100 GPUs: Throughput & MFU Normalization
equations.verbatimSummary: Synthesizes over 4,000 empirical distributed training scaling experiments across 1 to 512 H100 GPUs (1 to 64 nodes of 8xH100), normalizing throughput and Model FLOPS Utilization (MFU) across model scales (1B, 3B, 7B/8B, 70B/80B, 405B).
equations.engineApplication: Benchmarks GSE Coach-Brain LLM fine-tuning and distributed simulation throughput efficiency across multi-GPU nodes.

equations.title: Transformer Training Step Memory Anatomy & PyTorch Caching Allocator Dynamics
equations.equationLatex: M_{\text{total}}(t) = M_{\text{params}} + M_{\text{grads}}(t) + M_{\text{opt}} + M_{\text{act}}(t) + M_{\text{CUDA\_kernels}} + M_{\text{frag}}
equations.verbatimSummary: Decomposes time-varying GPU memory during a training step: forward pass builds activations M_act(t), backward pass accumulates gradients M_grads(t) while freeing activations, and step 1 transition allocates permanent Adam optimizer states M_opt (explaining why OOM often occurs on step 2 rather than step 1). CUDA kernels require 1-2 GB baseline.
equations.engineApplication: Prevents step-2 OOMs in GSE Mind trainer runs by pre-accounting for lazy Adam state initialization and PyTorch caching allocator block reservation.

equations.title: Transformer Parameter Count Quadratic Scaling Equation (Standard MLP)
equations.equationLatex: N_{\text{params}} = h \cdot v + L \cdot (12 h^2 + 13 h) + 2 h
equations.verbatimSummary: Exact parameter count for a standard dense Transformer with hidden dimension h, vocabulary size v, and L layers (tying input/output embeddings hv, 4h^2 attention QKV+O projections, 8h^2 MLP up/down projections, and 13h biases/LayerNorms). The 12 L h^2 term scales quadratically with hidden dimension h.
equations.engineApplication: Computes exact parameter budgets for dense Coach-Brain checkpoints prior to sharding.

equations.title: Transformer Parameter Count with Gated Linear Units (SwiGLU / Llama-3 Architecture)
equations.equationLatex: N_{\text{block,GLU}} = 4 h^2_{\text{attn}} + 12 h^2_{\text{GLU}} = 16 h^2, \quad N_{\text{model,GLU}} \approx 16 h^2 L + 2 h v
equations.verbatimSummary: Derives parameter count for modern SwiGLU/GLU Transformer blocks (such as Llama-3 and Qwen): Attention QKV (3h^2) + Output projection (h^2) = 4h^2; MLP Gate + Up projections (2 matrices of h x 4h = 8h^2) + Down projection (4h x h = 4h^2) = 12h^2; yielding 16h^2 parameters per layer.
equations.engineApplication: Provides exact layer-wise parameter sizing for Qwen3 / Llama-3 architectures used in GSE Mind & Neon AI Gateway.

equations.title: Full Precision (FP32) vs Mixed Precision (BF16 + FP32 Master Weights) Static Memory Equations
equations.verbatimSummary: Quantifies bytes per parameter Psi: FP32 training uses 4B weights + 4B grads + 8B Adam states = 16Psi bytes. Mixed precision (BF16 forward/backward) uses 2B BF16 weights + 2B BF16 grads + 4B FP32 master weights + 8B FP32 Adam momentum/variance = 16Psi bytes (or 20Psi bytes when accumulating gradients in FP32 for numerical stability, as in Nanotron): 1B=20GB, 7B=140GB, 70B=1400GB, 405B=8100GB.
equations.engineApplication: Governs static VRAM capacity planning for 1B-70B model weights, gradients, and FP32 master states.

equations.title: Exact Transformer Activation Memory Equation in Mixed Precision
equations.equationLatex: M_{\text{act}}^{\text{none}} = L \cdot s \cdot b \cdot h \left(34 + \frac{5 \cdot n_h \cdot s}{h}\right) \text{ bytes}
equations.verbatimSummary: Derives total forward activation memory saved for backward propagation in mixed precision without recomputation (following Korthikanti et al. 2022): scales linearly with layers L and micro-batch size b, and quadratically with sequence length s due to the attention score/dropout term (5 * n_h * s / h).
equations.engineApplication: Predicts activation memory explosion when scaling context length s for long-context corpus + game-log ingestion.

equations.title: Full Activation Recomputation (Gradient Checkpointing) Memory Bound & Compute Trade-off
equations.equationLatex: M_{\text{act}}^{\text{full}} = 2 \cdot L \cdot s \cdot b \cdot h \text{ bytes}, \quad C_{\text{FLOPs}}^{\text{full}} \approx \frac{4}{3} C_{\text{FLOPs}}^{\text{baseline}} \; (+30\%\text{--}40\%\text{ compute})
equations.verbatimSummary: Full activation recomputation checkpoints only the 2-byte BF16 hidden state (2*s*b*h bytes) at each of the L layer boundaries, discarding all intra-layer intermediate activations and recomputing a full forward pass per layer during backward propagation.
equations.engineApplication: Provides upper-bound memory compression for GPU-constrained training runs at the cost of +33% FLOPs overhead.

equations.title: Selective Activation Recomputation (Attention-Only Rematerialization & FlashAttention)
equations.equationLatex: M_{\text{act}}^{\text{selective}} = 34 \cdot L \cdot s \cdot b \cdot h \text{ bytes}, \quad \Delta M_{\text{act}} \approx -70\% \text{ at } \Delta C_{\text{FLOPs}} \approx +2.7\%
equations.verbatimSummary: Discards only the O(s^2) attention score/softmax/dropout activations (which have large memory footprint 5*n_h*s^2*b*L but cheap FLOPs) while keeping expensive feedforward (MLP) activations. On GPT-3 175B, achieves 70% activation memory reduction for only 2.7% extra compute; natively realized by FlashAttention.
equations.engineApplication: Default activation strategy in GSE Mind training: eliminates quadratic O(s^2) attention memory with negligible compute penalty.

equations.title: Hardware FLOPS Utilization (HFU) vs Model FLOPS Utilization (MFU)
equations.verbatimSummary: Distinguishes Model FLOPS Utilization (MFU, counting only required forward+backward operations independent of implementation) from Hardware FLOPS Utilization (HFU, which includes activation recomputation FLOPs). MFU rewards systems that avoid unnecessary recomputation and finish training faster.
equations.engineApplication: Standardizes benchmark reporting across GSE training jobs using MFU rather than inflated HFU.

equations.title: Gradient Accumulation & Global Batch Size Conservation Identity
equations.verbatimSummary: Splits a global batch into N_GAS sequential micro-batches of size b_micro, keeping peak activation memory independent of N_GAS while averaging accumulated gradients before the optimizer step.
equations.engineApplication: Allows exact target token batch sizes (e.g., 1M tokens/step) regardless of single-GPU micro-batch limits.

equations.title: Data Parallelism (DP) Three-Stage Overlap: Backward Hook, Gradient Bucketing, and no_sync
equations.verbatimSummary: Optimizes Data Parallelism via three mechanisms: (1) post-accumulate-grad backward hooks overlapping layer-l gradient AllReduce with layer-(l-1) backward compute; (2) bucketing gradients into ~25 MB contiguous buffers to amortize NCCL launch latency; and (3) disabling gradient sync via no_sync() on the first N_GAS - 1 micro-batches.
equations.engineApplication: Eliminates redundant inter-rank AllReduce communications during gradient accumulation steps.

equations.title: Critical Batch Size & Diminishing Returns of Pure Data Parallelism (McCandlish et al. 2018)
equations.verbatimSummary: Beyond the critical batch size B_crit determined by gradient noise scale, increasing DP degree to inflate global batch size B yields diminishing returns in convergence steps and wastes total training tokens.
equations.engineApplication: Caps batch-size scaling and motivates model/tensor/pipeline parallelism once B_global reaches the optimal token horizon.

equations.title: ZeRO-1 (Optimizer State Partitioning) Memory & Communication Equations
equations.verbatimSummary: Partitions FP32 master weights, FP32 gradient accumulators, and FP32 Adam momentum/variance (16Psi bytes total) across N_DP ranks while keeping full BF16 weights (2Psi) and BF16 gradients (2Psi). Replaces vanilla DP AllReduce (2Psi) with gradient ReduceScatter (Psi) + post-optimizer BF16 parameter AllGather (Psi), leaving total communication unchanged at 2Psi.
equations.engineApplication: Provides zero-overhead memory reduction (Combined with PP in DeepSeek-V3) with identical communication volume to DDP.

equations.title: ZeRO-2 (Optimizer + Gradient Partitioning) Memory & Communication Equations
equations.verbatimSummary: Extends ZeRO-1 by sharding BF16 gradients on the fly during backward pass via ReduceScatter, immediately freeing non-local gradient shards. Reduces static memory up to 8x as N_DP grows while maintaining the exact same 2Psi communication volume as ZeRO-1 and vanilla DP.
equations.engineApplication: Strictly dominates ZeRO-1 for pure data-parallel and TP+DP training up to 512 GPUs.

equations.title: ZeRO-3 / PyTorch FSDP (Full Parameter, Gradient & Optimizer Sharding) Memory & 3Psi Communication Tax
equations.verbatimSummary: Shards BF16 parameters, BF16 gradients, and FP32 master/optimizer states across N_DP ranks, gathering layer parameters on-demand in forward and backward passes and flushing immediately after use. Incurs 2*L-1 extra AllGathers per step (total volume 3Psi vs 2Psi for ZeRO-2), hidden via layer-(n+1) prefetching during layer-n compute up to DP <= 512.
equations.engineApplication: Enables fitting 70B+ models across nodes without model-code changes via FSDP layer prefetching.

equations.title: Tensor Parallelism (TP) Column-Linear vs Row-Linear Matrix Multiplication Algebra
equations.equationLatex: \text{Col-Parallel: } Y = X [W_1 \mid \cdots \mid W_p] = [X W_1 \mid \cdots \mid X W_p], \quad \text{Row-Parallel: } Y = [X_1 \mid \cdots \mid X_p] \begin{bmatrix} W_1 \\ \vdots \\ W_p \end{bmatrix} = \sum_{i=1}^p X_i W_i
equations.verbatimSummary: Proves the block-matrix identities underlying Megatron-LM Tensor Parallelism: ColumnParallelLinear splits weight columns W_i across TP ranks (producing column-sharded outputs Y_i without communication if X is synced), while RowParallelLinear splits weight rows W_i and takes column-sharded inputs X_i, summing partial products via AllReduce.
equations.engineApplication: Forms the mathematical core of intra-node sub-layer tensor sharding across NVLink GPUs.

equations.title: Transformer Block TP Pairing (MLP Column->Row & MHA Head-Sharded QKV->O) and GQA Constraints
equations.verbatimSummary: Pairs ColumnParallelLinear (up/gate projection or QKV projection) directly into RowParallelLinear (down projection or O projection) so element-wise GeLU/SwiGLU and per-head Softmax run locally without intermediate communication, requiring only 2 AllReduces per Transformer layer in forward and 2 in backward. Under Grouped Query Attention (GQA, e.g., Llama-3 8B with 32 Q heads and 8 KV heads), TP degree is bounded by N_KV_heads = 8 unless KV heads are replicated.
equations.engineApplication: Guides TP degree selection (TP <= 8 within single NVLink node, aligned with GQA KV head count).

equations.title: Sequence Parallelism (SP) Conjugate Operators (g, g*) & Peak Activation Memory Reduction
equations.equationLatex: g_{\text{fwd}} = \operatorname{AllGather}_{\text{seq}}, \quad g^*_{\text{fwd}} = \operatorname{ReduceScatter}_{\text{seq}}, \quad M_{\text{act,max}}^{\text{TP+SP}} = \frac{b \cdot s \cdot h}{N_{\text{TP}}} \text{ vs } M_{\text{act,max}}^{\text{TP}} = b \cdot s \cdot h
equations.verbatimSummary: Shards LayerNorm, Dropout, and residual additions along the sequence dimension (s / N_TP) outside the TP regions. Replaces each TP AllReduce (cost 2Psi_act) with conjugate pairs g (AllGather on SP->TP entry, cost Psi_act) and g* (ReduceScatter on TP->SP exit, cost Psi_act), reducing peak activation tensor shape from (b, s, h) to (b, s/N_TP, h) at zero additional communication volume.
equations.engineApplication: Mandatory companion to Tensor Parallelism: cuts LayerNorm/residual activation memory by N_TP with zero extra bandwidth cost.

equations.title: Sequence Parallel LayerNorm Full-Hidden-Dimension Requirement & Gradient Synchronization
equations.verbatimSummary: Because LayerNorm computes mean mu_h and variance sigma_h^2 across the full hidden dimension h, it cannot be sharded along h; SP shards it along s instead. Unlike vanilla TP (where LayerNorm inputs are identical across ranks), SP ranks see disjoint sequence slices s/N_TP, requiring a tiny AllReduce on LayerNorm parameter gradients (2h elements) during backward.
equations.engineApplication: Ensures exact mathematical equivalence between TP+SP and single-GPU training.

equations.title: Context Parallelism (CP) & Blockwise Ring Attention with Online Softmax
equations.equationLatex: m_i^{(t)} = \max\!\left(m_i^{(t-1)}, \max_j S_{ij}^{(t)}\right), \quad \ell_i^{(t)} = e^{m_i^{(t-1)} - m_i^{(t)}}\ell_i^{(t-1)} + \sum_j e^{S_{ij}^{(t)} - m_i^{(t)}}, \quad O_i^{(t)} = \operatorname{diag}(\ell_i^{(t)})^{-1}\!\left(\operatorname{diag}(\ell_i^{(t-1)})e^{m_i^{(t-1)} - m_i^{(t)}}O_i^{(t-1)} + e^{S_i^{(t)} - m_i^{(t)}}V^{(t)}\right)
equations.verbatimSummary: Splits sequences of length s (e.g., 128k+ tokens) into s / N_CP chunks across N_CP GPUs throughout the entire model. In attention layers, each GPU asynchronously sends its local (K, V) chunk to rank (r+1) mod N_CP while computing blockwise attention and updating online softmax running max m_i and normalizer l_i over N_CP ring steps.
equations.engineApplication: Enables 128k+ long-context training and inference without materializing full sequence activations on any single GPU.

equations.title: Zig-Zag Ring Attention Load Balancing Under Causal Masking
equations.equationLatex: \mathcal{I}_r^{\text{ZigZag}} = \left[\frac{r \cdot s}{2 N_{\text{CP}}}, \frac{(r+1)s}{2 N_{\text{CP}}}\right) \cup \left[\frac{(2N_{\text{CP}} - 1 - r)s}{2 N_{\text{CP}}}, \frac{(2N_{\text{CP}} - r)s}{2 N_{\text{CP}}}\right), \quad W_r = \frac{s^2}{2 N_{\text{CP}}} \;\forall r
equations.verbatimSummary: Resolves the severe causal-mask compute imbalance of naive sequential Ring Attention (where rank 0 only computes 1/(2 N_CP) triangle while rank N_CP-1 computes (2 N_CP - 1)/(2 N_CP)) by assigning each rank r one symmetric early token chunk and one late token chunk, equalizing non-masked causal attention FLOPs across all N_CP ranks.
equations.engineApplication: Eliminates straggler ranks in causal long-context attention across CP process groups.

equations.title: Pipeline Parallelism (PP) Naive vs All-Forward-All-Backward (AFAB) Bubble Ratio & Activation Memory
equations.equationLatex: r_{\text{bubble}}^{\text{naive}} = \frac{(p - 1)(t_f + t_b)}{t_f + t_b} = p - 1, \quad r_{\text{bubble}}^{\text{AFAB}} = \frac{(p - 1)(t_f + t_b)}{m(t_f + t_b)} = \frac{p - 1}{m}, \quad M_{\text{act}}^{\text{AFAB}} = m \cdot M_{\text{act,stage}}
equations.verbatimSummary: Quantifies the idle pipeline bubble fraction across p pipeline stages and m micro-batches: splitting a batch into m micro-batches under AFAB reduces the bubble fraction from p-1 to (p-1)/m, but requires storing activations for all m micro-batches simultaneously until the backward phase begins.
equations.engineApplication: Establishes the fundamental bubble-vs-memory law of multi-node pipeline parallelism.

equations.title: 1F1B (One-Forward-One-Backward) Steady-State Schedule & Activation Memory Cap
equations.equationLatex: r_{\text{bubble}}^{\text{1F1B}} = \frac{p - 1}{m}, \quad N_{\text{warmup}}(r) = \min(p - r - 1, m), \quad M_{\text{act}}^{\text{1F1B}} = p \cdot M_{\text{act,stage}} \ll m \cdot M_{\text{act,stage}}
equations.verbatimSummary: Transitions each pipeline stage r after p-r-1 warmup forward micro-batches into a steady state alternating 1 forward and 1 backward micro-batch, immediately freeing activations after each backward step. Caps peak stored activations at p micro-batches instead of m, allowing large m >> p to shrink the pipeline bubble. Cross-node scaling from p=8 (1 node) to p=16 (2 nodes) drops throughput by only 14% vs 43% for cross-node TP.
equations.engineApplication: Explains why PP out-scales TP across slower inter-node interconnects (EFA/RoCE/InfiniBand).

equations.title: Interleaved Pipeline Parallelism (Looping Pipeline / Llama-3.1 Depth-First vs Breadth-First)
equations.verbatimSummary: Assigns v non-contiguous model chunks (virtual stages, e.g., odd/even layers) per GPU so micro-batches loop through the pipeline v times. Reduces stage compute duration and bubble fraction by a factor of v at the cost of v-fold increase in P2P activation transfers; tunable between depth-first (finish micro-batches early to free memory) and breadth-first (fill pipeline early) as used in Llama-3.1.
equations.engineApplication: Trades moderate P2P bandwidth for a 1/v reduction in pipeline idle bubble.

equations.title: Zero-Bubble Pipeline Parallelism (B / W Backward Split) & DeepSeek-V3 Bidirectional DualPipe
equations.equationLatex:
abla_X \mathcal{L} = (
abla_Y \mathcal{L}) W^	op \;\;(	ext{op } B), \quad 
abla_W \mathcal{L} = X^	op (
abla_Y \mathcal{L}) \;\;(	ext{op } W), \quad r_{	ext{bubble}}^{	ext{ZB-H2 / DualPipe}} 	o 0
equations.verbatimSummary: Decomposes backward matrix multiplication into input-gradient B (on the critical path for stage r-1) and weight-gradient W (only needed before the optimizer step, freely schedulable into pipeline bubbles via ILP). DeepSeek-V3 DualPipe extends B/W splitting with two bidirectional micro-batch streams from both ends of the pipeline, overlapping forward and backward compute with all-to-all MoE communication for near-zero bubble and near-zero communication overhead.
equations.engineApplication: State-of-the-art pipeline scheduling reference for MoE + multi-node LLM training.

equations.title: Mixture of Experts (MoE) & Expert Parallelism (EP) All-to-All Routing with Node-Limited Routing
equations.verbatimSummary: Distributes independent MoE feedforward experts across N_EP workers and routes token hidden states via All-to-All collectives while combining with DP for non-MoE layers. DeepSeek-V3 (256 experts) constrains router dispatch so each token is sent to at most M=4 nodes, bounding inter-node All-to-All communication.
equations.engineApplication: Governs sparse expert routing and node-locality constraints in MoE architectures.

equations.title: 5D Parallelism Composition Law & ZeRO-3 vs Pipeline Parallelism Duality Theorem
equations.equationLatex: N_{\text{GPUs}} = N_{\text{DP}} \times N_{\text{CP}} \times N_{\text{TP}} \times N_{\text{PP}}, \quad N_{\text{DP\_total}} = N_{\text{DP}} \times N_{\text{EP}} \text{ (for MoE layers)}
equations.verbatimSummary: Unifies all five orthogonal axes—DP (batch), TP+SP (hidden/seq), CP (long context seq), PP (depth layers), and EP (MoE experts)—plus ZeRO-1/2/3. Establishes the duality between ZeRO-3 (stores fractional layer, communicates weights O(h^2), prefers large b*s to hide comms) and PP (stores full layer, communicates activations O(b*s*h), prefers large GAS to hide bubble), explaining why PP + ZeRO-1/2 + intra-node TP+SP is preferred at 1,024+ GPUs.
equations.engineApplication: Master architectural taxonomy for mapping any LLM onto multi-node GPU clusters.

equations.title: 3-Step Hierarchical 5D Parallelism Configuration Solver & 4,000-Run Heatmap Optima
equations.equationLatex: \max_{(N_{\text{TP}}, N_{\text{PP}}, N_{\text{DP}}, N_{\text{CP}}, b, N_{\text{GAS}}, \text{ZeRO})} \text{MFU} \quad \text{s.t.} \quad M_{\text{peak}} \le M_{\text{HBM}}, \;\; b \cdot s \cdot N_{\text{GAS}} \cdot N_{\text{DP}} = B_{\text{target}}, \;\; N_{\text{TP}} \le 8
equations.verbatimSummary: Formulates the 3-step optimal configuration algorithm validated across 1-64 nodes of 8xH100 (s=4096, B_target=1M tokens): Step 1 Fit in memory (<=10B: TP or ZeRO-3 on 8 GPUs; 10B-100B: TP=8 + PP or TP=8 + ZeRO-3; 512+ GPUs: add PP; 1024+ GPUs: TP=8 + PP + ZeRO-2); Step 2 Hit target global batch size via DP/GAS/CP; Step 3 Maximize MFU by keeping TP<=8 intra-node NVLink and balancing micro-batch size b.
equations.engineApplication: Provides deterministic configuration rules for cluster job sizing.

equations.title: NVIDIA H100 Hopper GPU Compute & Memory Hierarchy Specification
equations.verbatimSummary: Characterizes the hierarchical execution model: 32 threads form a lock-step SIMD warp; warps form thread blocks scheduled onto 132 Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs); memory bandwidth degrades from per-thread registers to per-SM Shared Memory/L1 SRAM, cross-SM L2 cache, and 80 GB HBM global memory. Note: NCCL communication kernels consume SMs, causing compute-communication SM contention.
equations.engineApplication: Informs custom kernel block sizing and NCCL SM allocation during overlapped communication.

equations.title: Kernel Compilation Hierarchy: PyTorch Eager vs @torch.compile vs Triton JIT vs CUDA C++
equations.verbatimSummary: Demonstrates how @torch.compile captures PyTorch graphs and emits fused Triton kernels (inspectable via TORCH_LOGS="output_code"), eliminating intermediate HBM reads/writes for pointwise ops like ELU, while custom CUDA unlocks warp-level shared-memory and SM scheduling beyond block-level Triton.
equations.engineApplication: Guides kernel optimization workflow: start with @torch.compile, refine in Triton, drop to CUDA only for warp/SM-level bottlenecks.

equations.title: DRAM Burst Memory Coalescing in Row-Major Matrix Multiplication (10x Speedup)
equations.equationLatex: x = \text{blockIdx.x} \cdot B + \lfloor \text{threadIdx.x} / B \rfloor, \quad y = \text{blockIdx.y} \cdot B + (\text{threadIdx.x} \bmod B) \implies \text{Address}(B_{i,y}) = i \cdot N + y \text{ (contiguous across warp)}
equations.verbatimSummary: Proves why naive 2D thread-to-index mapping (x = blockIdx.x*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x) causes uncoalesced strided DRAM accesses on row-major matrices (adjacent threads in a warp vary x and read column elements separated by stride K). Remapping threadIdx.x mod B to column index y aligns warp threads to consecutive memory addresses, yielding a measured 10x increase in HBM throughput and 10x reduction in kernel time.
equations.engineApplication: Critical rule for all custom GPU tensor kernels: consecutive threadIdx.x within a 32-thread warp must index contiguous inner-dimension memory.

equations.title: Shared-Memory Tiled Matrix Multiplication & HBM Bandwidth Reduction
equations.equationLatex: C_{\text{tile}} = \sum_{t=0}^{K / T - 1} A_{\text{shared}}^{(t)} B_{\text{shared}}^{(t)}, \quad \text{HBM Reads Reduction} = \mathcal{O}\!\left(\frac{1}{T}\right) \implies 410\text{ GB/s},\; 6.6\text{ TFLOPS}\; (-43\%\text{ time})
equations.verbatimSummary: Cooperatively loads T x T tiles of A and B from slow HBM into fast per-SM Shared Memory once per tile step (synchronized via __syncthreads()), reusing each loaded element T times across the thread block and cutting global memory traffic by factor T.
equations.engineApplication: Foundation of block-tiled GEMM and attention kernels.

equations.title: Thread Coarsening (MIO Stall Mitigation) & Warp SIMD Control Divergence Elimination
equations.verbatimSummary: Resolves Nsight Compute MIO (Memory Input/Output) instruction queue stalls on shared memory by coarsening each thread to compute multiple output elements via wider vector loads, and eliminates SIMD warp serialization by avoiding divergent branch conditionals within 32-thread warps.
equations.engineApplication: Used when profiling custom CUDA kernels with `ncu --set full`.

equations.title: Kernel Fusion & FlashAttention-1/2/3 IO-Aware Exact Tiled Attention in SRAM
equations.equationLatex: S = Q K^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{s \times s} \text{ (never materialized in HBM)}, \quad M_{\text{HBM\_IO}}^{\text{Flash}} = \Theta\!\left(\frac{s^2 d^2}{M_{\text{SRAM}}}\right) \ll \Theta(s^2 + s d)
equations.verbatimSummary: Fuses QK^T, online softmax scaling, dropout, and PV multiplication into a single SRAM-resident tiled kernel without materializing the N x N attention matrix S or P in HBM, plus native selective activation recomputation in backward. FlashAttention-2 optimizes warp/thread-block partitioning and minimizes non-matmul FLOPs; FlashAttention-3 adds Hopper H100 asynchronous WGMMA Tensor Core and FP8 support.
equations.engineApplication: Explains how exact O(s^2) attention runs at near-peak Tensor Core FLOPS with O(s) memory.

equations.title: Floating-Point Representation Anatomy & Resolution Epsilon (FP32, FP16, BF16, FP8 E4M3, FP8 E5M2)
equations.verbatimSummary: Catalogs bit allocations (Sign, Exponent, Mantissa) and interval [1,2] resolution across 5 formats: FP32 (1/8/23, 80 orders of magnitude), FP16 (1/5/10, narrow dynamic range causing overflow/underflow), BF16 (1/8/7, full FP32 dynamic range at lower mantissa precision), FP8 E4M3 (1/4/3, 7 points in [1,2], higher precision for forward/weights), and FP8 E5M2 (1/5/2, 3 points in [1,2], wider range for gradients).
equations.engineApplication: Numerical foundation for mixed-precision and quantized inference/training.

equations.title: Three Pillars of Mixed Precision Stability: FP32 Master Weights, Dynamic Loss Scaling, FP32 Accumulators
equations.verbatimSummary: Prevents gradient underflow and weight update swamping (where |Delta w| < epsilon_BF16 * |w| rounds to zero in 16-bit) via (1) maintaining FP32 master weights for updates, (2) scaling loss by alpha_scale before backward and unscaling gradients before clipping/optimizer, and (3) accumulating reductions in FP32.
equations.engineApplication: Prevents silent weight stagnation and NaN/Inf divergence in mixed-precision training.

equations.title: FP8 Pretraining Memory & Precision Comparison (Transformer Engine, FP8-LM O3, DeepSeek-V3, Nanotron FP8)
equations.equationLatex: S_{\text{tile}}^{1\times 128}(X) = \frac{\max_{j \in [1,128]} |X_{i,j}|}{V_{\max}^{\text{E4M3}}}, \quad M_{\text{static}} = \begin{cases} 20\Psi & \text{BF16 + FP32 grad acc} \\ 16\Psi & \text{BF16 no FP32 grad acc / TE FP8} \\ 15\Psi & \text{DeepSeek-V3 FP8 (25\% save)} \\ 10\Psi & \text{Nanotron FP8 (50\% save)} \\ 9\Psi & \text{FP8-LM O3 (55\% save)} \end{cases}
equations.verbatimSummary: Compares H100 FP8 GEMM (2x theoretical FLOPS of BF16) across production schemes (Table I, p. 199): DeepSeek-V3 achieves stable large-scale FP8 pretraining via fine-grained 1x128 per-token activation tile scaling and 128x128 weight block scaling with FP32 master weights, FP32 accumulated gradients, FP8 model weights, BF16 gradients, and BF16+BF16 Adam states (15 bytes/param, 25% memory reduction). Nanotron FP8 uses BF16 master weights and FP8 optimizer states (10 bytes/param, 50% reduction).
equations.engineApplication: Directly guides FP8 quantization and tile-wise outlier normalization on Hopper/Blackwell GPUs.

equations.title: Collective Communication Primitives & Ring AllReduce Bandwidth Optimality Theorem
equations.verbatimSummary: Derives the exact per-GPU data transfer volume of Ring AllReduce across N GPUs: phase 1 (ReduceScatter) sends N-1 chunks of size Psi/N around the ring (cost (N-1)/N * Psi); phase 2 (AllGather) circulates the reduced shards (cost (N-1)/N * Psi). Proves ReduceScatter and AllGather each cost exactly half of an AllReduce (~Psi vs ~2Psi) and saturate link bandwidth independent of N.
equations.engineApplication: Fundamental collective cost model used throughout ZeRO, DP, TP, and SP communication accounting.

equations.title: Asynchronous CUDA Event Timing, PyTorch Profiler Schedules & Nsight Compute (ncu) Diagnostics
equations.verbatimSummary: Demonstrates why Python `time.time()` only measures asynchronous CPU kernel launch overhead rather than GPU execution, and provides exact protocols for `torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)`, `torch.profiler.schedule(wait=1, warmup=3, active=2)`, `ncu --set full`, and `torch.utils.cpp_extension.load`.
equations.engineApplication: Standardizes accurate GPU latency and kernel occupancy profiling across GSE ML services.

equations.title: Transformer Forward & Backward FLOPs Scaling Law (Linear 6ND + Quadratic Attention Term)
equations.equationLatex: C_{\text{fwd}} \approx 2 b s N_{\text{params}}, \quad C_{\text{bwd}} \approx 4 b s N_{\text{params}}, \quad C_{\text{fwd+bwd}}^{\text{exact}} = 6 b s N_{\text{params}} + 12 b L h s^2
equations.verbatimSummary: Establishes the canonical compute formulas: forward pass requires ~2*b*s*(16 L h^2) FLOPs, backward pass requires twice forward (~4*b*s*(16 L h^2) FLOPs for Dgrad + Wgrad), and exact forward+backward includes the quadratic attention term 12*b*L*h*s^2 (negligible when s << 8h, dominant at ultra-long context s >> 8h).
equations.engineApplication: Used to compute exact MFU and compute-to-communication overlap ratios across all sequence lengths.

equations.title: Data Parallelism (ZeRO-0) Compute-to-Communication Overlap Ratio rho_DP
equations.equationLatex: T_{\text{comm}}^{\text{DP}} = \frac{4 \cdot 16 h^2 L}{\text{BW}_{\text{AllReduce}}}, \quad T_{\text{comp}}^{\text{bwd}} = \frac{2 \cdot 2 b s \cdot 16 h^2 L}{\text{FLOPS}_{\text{GPU}}}, \quad \rho_{\text{DP}} = \frac{T_{\text{comm}}^{\text{DP}}}{T_{\text{comp}}^{\text{bwd}}} = \frac{\text{FLOPS}_{\text{GPU}}}{b \cdot s \cdot \text{BW}_{\text{AllReduce}}} < 1
equations.verbatimSummary: Derives the exact dimensionless overlap ratio rho_DP for Data Parallelism: communication is fully hidden behind backward pass computation iff rho_DP = FLOPS_GPU / (b * s * BW_AllReduce) < 1, which depends only on tokens per micro-batch (b * s) and hardware FLOPS-to-bandwidth ratio, independent of model depth L or hidden size h.
equations.engineApplication: Determines the minimum micro-batch token count (b * s) required to hide DP gradient synchronization.

equations.title: ZeRO-3 / FSDP Compute-to-Communication Overlap Ratio rho_ZeRO3
equations.equationLatex: T_{\text{comm}}^{\text{ZeRO-3,block}} = \frac{2 \cdot 16 h^2}{\text{BW}_{\text{AllGather}}}, \quad T_{\text{comp}}^{\text{fwd,block}} = \frac{2 b s \cdot 16 h^2}{\text{FLOPS}_{\text{GPU}}}, \quad \rho_{\text{ZeRO-3}} = \frac{T_{\text{comm}}^{\text{ZeRO-3,block}}}{T_{\text{comp}}^{\text{fwd,block}}} = \frac{\text{FLOPS}_{\text{GPU}}}{b \cdot s \cdot \text{BW}_{\text{AllGather}}} < 1
equations.verbatimSummary: Derives the per-block communication volume for ZeRO-3 (2*16h^2 bytes fwd AllGather + 2*16h^2 bytes bwd AllGather + 2*16h^2 bytes bwd ReduceScatter = 6*16h^2 bytes/block) and proves that prefetching layer n+1 weights hides behind layer n forward compute iff rho_ZeRO3 = FLOPS_GPU / (b * s * BW_AllGather) < 1.
equations.engineApplication: Explains why ZeRO-3 requires large token micro-batches (b * s) to avoid exposed inter-node AllGather stalls.

equations.title: Tensor Parallelism (TP+SP) Compute-to-Communication Overlap Ratio rho_TP
equations.equationLatex: V_{\text{comm}}^{\text{TP,block}} = 8 b s h \frac{N_{\text{TP}} - 1}{N_{\text{TP}}}, \quad \rho_{\text{TP}} = \frac{T_{\text{comm}}^{\text{AllGather}}}{T_{\text{comp}}^{\text{linear}}} = \frac{b s h \frac{N_{\text{TP}} - 1}{N_{\text{TP}}} / \text{BW}_{\text{AllGather}}}{8 b s h^2 / (N_{\text{TP}} \cdot \text{FLOPS}_{\text{GPU}})} = \frac{(N_{\text{TP}} - 1)\,\text{FLOPS}_{\text{GPU}}}{8 h \cdot \text{BW}_{\text{AllGather}}} < 1
equations.verbatimSummary: Derives the per-block TP+SP communication volume (8*b*s*h*(N_TP - 1)/N_TP bytes across 2 column-linear and 2 row-linear ops) and proves that overlapping AllGather with the next linear layer (8h^2 parameters) depends ONLY on hidden dimension h and TP degree N_TP—completely independent of batch size b and sequence length s!
equations.engineApplication: Crucial theorem: increasing batch size b or sequence length s NEVER helps hide TP communication; only larger hidden size h or faster NVLink bandwidth helps.

equations.title: Pipeline Parallelism (PP) P2P Compute-to-Communication Overlap Ratio rho_PP
equations.equationLatex: V_{\text{comm}}^{\text{PP,step}} = 4 \cdot N_{\text{GAS}} \cdot b s h, \quad \rho_{\text{PP}} = \frac{T_{\text{comm}}^{\text{P2P}}}{T_{\text{comp}}^{\text{stage}}} = \frac{2 b s h / \text{BW}_{\text{P2P}}}{2 b s \cdot 16 h^2 L_{\text{stage}} / \text{FLOPS}_{\text{GPU}}} = \frac{\text{FLOPS}_{\text{GPU}}}{16 h \cdot L_{\text{stage}} \cdot \text{BW}_{\text{P2P}}} < 1
equations.verbatimSummary: Derives total P2P activation/gradient transfer per micro-batch (4*b*s*h bytes across fwd+bwd) and proves that overlapping P2P transfer with the next stage compute (L_stage layers) depends ONLY on hidden size h, layers per stage L_stage, and P2P bandwidth—independent of b and s, and suppressed by 1/(16 * h * L_stage).
equations.engineApplication: Proves why PP easily overlaps inter-node communication whenever each stage holds multiple layers L_stage >= 2.

equations.title: DeepSeek-V3 Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA) & Low-Rank KV Compression
equations.equationLatex: c_t^{KV} = W^{DKV} h_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d_c}, \quad d_c \ll n_h d_h, \quad \text{KV Activation Footprint} \propto b \cdot s \cdot d_c
equations.verbatimSummary: Highlights how DeepSeek-V3 compresses attention Keys and Values into a low-rank latent vector c_t^KV before caching/checkpointing, drastically shrinking activation memory during selective recomputation and long-context training.
equations.engineApplication: Informs low-rank KV state compression in GSE long-horizon play-by-play sequence models.

equations.title: Multi-Query Attention (MQA) & Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) Parameter & KV-Bandwidth Scaling
equations.equationLatex: N_{\text{QKV}}^{\text{GQA}} = h^2 \left(1 + \frac{2 N_{\text{KV}}}{N_Q}\right), \quad V_{\text{KV\_comm}}^{\text{CP}} \propto 2 b s \cdot \frac{N_{\text{KV}}}{N_Q} h
equations.verbatimSummary: Reduces Key/Value projection parameters and Context Parallel Ring Attention KV communication volume by factor N_KV / N_Q (e.g., 8/32 = 0.25x in Llama-3 8B) while preserving multi-head query expressivity.
equations.engineApplication: Explains how GQA accelerates both Ring Attention CP communication during training and KV-cache bandwidth during inference.

equations.title: Pipeline Parallel Gradient Synchronization Gating on Final Micro-Batch Only
equations.verbatimSummary: In hybrid PP + DP training (1F1B or AFAB), DP gradient AllReduce/ReduceScatter must be suppressed on all warmup and steady-state micro-batches and triggered strictly on the final cooldown micro-batch of each stage, preventing p-fold redundant DP synchronizations.
equations.engineApplication: Prevents catastrophic AllReduce deadlocks and redundant synchronization in hybrid PP+DP schedules.

equations.title: Embedding & LM-Head Vocabulary Parallelism (Row/Column TP + SP ReduceScatter)
equations.verbatimSummary: Shards the input token embedding table (v x h) row-wise across vocabulary slices v/N_TP and exits directly into the SP region via ReduceScatter along the sequence dimension (instead of AllReduce in vanilla TP), while sharding the output LM head column-wise to compute distributed cross-entropy without materializing full (b, s, v) logits.

equations.engineApplication: Benchmarks GSE Coach-Brain LLM fine-tuning and distributed simulation throughput efficiency across multi-GPU nodes.

equations.title: Transformer Training Step Memory Anatomy & PyTorch Caching Allocator Dynamics
equations.equationLatex: M_{\text{total}}(t) = M_{\text{params}} + M_{\text{grads}}(t) + M_{\text{opt}} + M_{\text{act}}(t) + M_{\text{CUDA\_kernels}} + M_{\text{frag}}
equations.verbatimSummary: Decomposes time-varying GPU memory during a training step: forward pass builds activations M_act(t), backward pass accumulates gradients M_grads(t) while freeing activations, and step 1 transition allocates permanent Adam optimizer states M_opt (explaining why OOM often occurs on step 2 rather than step 1). CUDA kernels require 1-2 GB baseline.
equations.engineApplication: Prevents step-2 OOMs in GSE Mind trainer runs by pre-accounting for lazy Adam state initialization and PyTorch caching allocator block reservation.

equations.title: Transformer Parameter Count Quadratic Scaling Equation (Standard MLP)
equations.equationLatex: N_{\text{params}} = h \cdot v + L \cdot (12 h^2 + 13 h) + 2 h
equations.verbatimSummary: Exact parameter count for a standard dense Transformer with hidden dimension h, vocabulary size v, and L layers (tying input/output embeddings hv, 4h^2 attention QKV+O projections, 8h^2 MLP up/down projections, and 13h biases/LayerNorms). The 12 L h^2 term scales quadratically with hidden dimension h.
equations.engineApplication: Computes exact parameter budgets for dense Coach-Brain checkpoints prior to sharding.

equations.title: Transformer Parameter Count with Gated Linear Units (SwiGLU / Llama-3 Architecture)
equations.equationLatex: N_{\text{block,GLU}} = 4 h^2_{\text{attn}} + 12 h^2_{\text{GLU}} = 16 h^2, \quad N_{\text{model,GLU}} \approx 16 h^2 L + 2 h v
equations.verbatimSummary: Derives parameter count for modern SwiGLU/GLU Transformer blocks (such as Llama-3 and Qwen): Attention QKV (3h^2) + Output projection (h^2) = 4h^2; MLP Gate + Up projections (2 matrices of h x 4h = 8h^2) + Down projection (4h x h = 4h^2) = 12h^2; yielding 16h^2 parameters per layer.
equations.engineApplication: Provides exact layer-wise parameter sizing for Qwen3 / Llama-3 architectures used in GSE Mind & Neon AI Gateway.

equations.title: Full Precision (FP32) vs Mixed Precision (BF16 + FP32 Master Weights) Static Memory Equations
equations.verbatimSummary: Quantifies bytes per parameter Psi: FP32 training uses 4B weights + 4B grads + 8B Adam states = 16Psi bytes. Mixed precision (BF16 forward/backward) uses 2B BF16 weights + 2B BF16 grads + 4B FP32 master weights + 8B FP32 Adam momentum/variance = 16Psi bytes (or 20Psi bytes when accumulating gradients in FP32 for numerical stability, as in Nanotron): 1B=20GB, 7B=140GB, 70B=1400GB, 405B=8100GB.
equations.engineApplication: Governs static VRAM capacity planning for 1B-70B model weights, gradients, and FP32 master states.

equations.title: Exact Transformer Activation Memory Equation in Mixed Precision
equations.equationLatex: M_{\text{act}}^{\text{none}} = L \cdot s \cdot b \cdot h \left(34 + \frac{5 \cdot n_h \cdot s}{h}\right) \text{ bytes}
equations.verbatimSummary: Derives total forward activation memory saved for backward propagation in mixed precision without recomputation (following Korthikanti et al. 2022): scales linearly with layers L and micro-batch size b, and quadratically with sequence length s due to the attention score/dropout term (5 * n_h * s / h).
equations.engineApplication: Predicts activation memory explosion when scaling context length s for long-context corpus + game-log ingestion.

equations.title: Full Activation Recomputation (Gradient Checkpointing) Memory Bound & Compute Trade-off
equations.equationLatex: M_{\text{act}}^{\text{full}} = 2 \cdot L \cdot s \cdot b \cdot h \text{ bytes}, \quad C_{\text{FLOPs}}^{\text{full}} \approx \frac{4}{3} C_{\text{FLOPs}}^{\text{baseline}} \; (+30\%\text{--}40\%\text{ compute})
equations.verbatimSummary: Full activation recomputation checkpoints only the 2-byte BF16 hidden state (2*s*b*h bytes) at each of the L layer boundaries, discarding all intra-layer intermediate activations and recomputing a full forward pass per layer during backward propagation.
equations.engineApplication: Provides upper-bound memory compression for GPU-constrained training runs at the cost of +33% FLOPs overhead.

equations.title: Selective Activation Recomputation (Attention-Only Rematerialization & FlashAttention)
equations.equationLatex: M_{\text{act}}^{\text{selective}} = 34 \cdot L \cdot s \cdot b \cdot h \text{ bytes}, \quad \Delta M_{\text{act}} \approx -70\% \text{ at } \Delta C_{\text{FLOPs}} \approx +2.7\%
equations.verbatimSummary: Discards only the O(s^2) attention score/softmax/dropout activations (which have large memory footprint 5*n_h*s^2*b*L but cheap FLOPs) while keeping expensive feedforward (MLP) activations. On GPT-3 175B, achieves 70% activation memory reduction for only 2.7% extra compute; natively realized by FlashAttention.
equations.engineApplication: Default activation strategy in GSE Mind training: eliminates quadratic O(s^2) attention memory with negligible compute penalty.

equations.title: Hardware FLOPS Utilization (HFU) vs Model FLOPS Utilization (MFU)
equations.verbatimSummary: Distinguishes Model FLOPS Utilization (MFU, counting only required forward+backward operations independent of implementation) from Hardware FLOPS Utilization (HFU, which includes activation recomputation FLOPs). MFU rewards systems that avoid unnecessary recomputation and finish training faster.
equations.engineApplication: Standardizes benchmark reporting across GSE training jobs using MFU rather than inflated HFU.

equations.title: Gradient Accumulation & Global Batch Size Conservation Identity
equations.verbatimSummary: Splits a global batch into N_GAS sequential micro-batches of size b_micro, keeping peak activation memory independent of N_GAS while averaging accumulated gradients before the optimizer step.
equations.engineApplication: Allows exact target token batch sizes (e.g., 1M tokens/step) regardless of single-GPU micro-batch limits.

equations.title: Data Parallelism (DP) Three-Stage Overlap: Backward Hook, Gradient Bucketing, and no_sync
equations.verbatimSummary: Optimizes Data Parallelism via three mechanisms: (1) post-accumulate-grad backward hooks overlapping layer-l gradient AllReduce with layer-(l-1) backward compute; (2) bucketing gradients into ~25 MB contiguous buffers to amortize NCCL launch latency; and (3) disabling gradient sync via no_sync() on the first N_GAS - 1 micro-batches.
equations.engineApplication: Eliminates redundant inter-rank AllReduce communications during gradient accumulation steps.

equations.title: Critical Batch Size & Diminishing Returns of Pure Data Parallelism (McCandlish et al. 2018)
equations.verbatimSummary: Beyond the critical batch size B_crit determined by gradient noise scale, increasing DP degree to inflate global batch size B yields diminishing returns in convergence steps and wastes total training tokens.
equations.engineApplication: Caps batch-size scaling and motivates model/tensor/pipeline parallelism once B_global reaches the optimal token horizon.

equations.title: ZeRO-1 (Optimizer State Partitioning) Memory & Communication Equations
equations.verbatimSummary: Partitions FP32 master weights, FP32 gradient accumulators, and FP32 Adam momentum/variance (16Psi bytes total) across N_DP ranks while keeping full BF16 weights (2Psi) and BF16 gradients (2Psi). Replaces vanilla DP AllReduce (2Psi) with gradient ReduceScatter (Psi) + post-optimizer BF16 parameter AllGather (Psi), leaving total communication unchanged at 2Psi.
equations.engineApplication: Provides zero-overhead memory reduction (Combined with PP in DeepSeek-V3) with identical communication volume to DDP.

equations.title: ZeRO-2 (Optimizer + Gradient Partitioning) Memory & Communication Equations
equations.verbatimSummary: Extends ZeRO-1 by sharding BF16 gradients on the fly during backward pass via ReduceScatter, immediately freeing non-local gradient shards. Reduces static memory up to 8x as N_DP grows while maintaining the exact same 2Psi communication volume as ZeRO-1 and vanilla DP.
equations.engineApplication: Strictly dominates ZeRO-1 for pure data-parallel and TP+DP training up to 512 GPUs.

equations.title: ZeRO-3 / PyTorch FSDP (Full Parameter, Gradient & Optimizer Sharding) Memory & 3Psi Communication Tax
equations.verbatimSummary: Shards BF16 parameters, BF16 gradients, and FP32 master/optimizer states across N_DP ranks, gathering layer parameters on-demand in forward and backward passes and flushing immediately after use. Incurs 2*L-1 extra AllGathers per step (total volume 3Psi vs 2Psi for ZeRO-2), hidden via layer-(n+1) prefetching during layer-n compute up to DP <= 512.
equations.engineApplication: Enables fitting 70B+ models across nodes without model-code changes via FSDP layer prefetching.

equations.title: Tensor Parallelism (TP) Column-Linear vs Row-Linear Matrix Multiplication Algebra
equations.equationLatex: \text{Col-Parallel: } Y = X [W_1 \mid \cdots \mid W_p] = [X W_1 \mid \cdots \mid X W_p], \quad \text{Row-Parallel: } Y = [X_1 \mid \cdots \mid X_p] \begin{bmatrix} W_1 \\ \vdots \\ W_p \end{bmatrix} = \sum_{i=1}^p X_i W_i
equations.verbatimSummary: Proves the block-matrix identities underlying Megatron-LM Tensor Parallelism: ColumnParallelLinear splits weight columns W_i across TP ranks (producing column-sharded outputs Y_i without communication if X is synced), while RowParallelLinear splits weight rows W_i and takes column-sharded inputs X_i, summing partial products via AllReduce.
equations.engineApplication: Forms the mathematical core of intra-node sub-layer tensor sharding across NVLink GPUs.

equations.title: Transformer Block TP Pairing (MLP Column->Row & MHA Head-Sharded QKV->O) and GQA Constraints
equations.verbatimSummary: Pairs ColumnParallelLinear (up/gate projection or QKV projection) directly into RowParallelLinear (down projection or O projection) so element-wise GeLU/SwiGLU and per-head Softmax run locally without intermediate communication, requiring only 2 AllReduces per Transformer layer in forward and 2 in backward. Under Grouped Query Attention (GQA, e.g., Llama-3 8B with 32 Q heads and 8 KV heads), TP degree is bounded by N_KV_heads = 8 unless KV heads are replicated.
equations.engineApplication: Guides TP degree selection (TP <= 8 within single NVLink node, aligned with GQA KV head count).

equations.title: Sequence Parallelism (SP) Conjugate Operators (g, g*) & Peak Activation Memory Reduction
equations.equationLatex: g_{\text{fwd}} = \operatorname{AllGather}_{\text{seq}}, \quad g^*_{\text{fwd}} = \operatorname{ReduceScatter}_{\text{seq}}, \quad M_{\text{act,max}}^{\text{TP+SP}} = \frac{b \cdot s \cdot h}{N_{\text{TP}}} \text{ vs } M_{\text{act,max}}^{\text{TP}} = b \cdot s \cdot h
equations.verbatimSummary: Shards LayerNorm, Dropout, and residual additions along the sequence dimension (s / N_TP) outside the TP regions. Replaces each TP AllReduce (cost 2Psi_act) with conjugate pairs g (AllGather on SP->TP entry, cost Psi_act) and g* (ReduceScatter on TP->SP exit, cost Psi_act), reducing peak activation tensor shape from (b, s, h) to (b, s/N_TP, h) at zero additional communication volume.
equations.engineApplication: Mandatory companion to Tensor Parallelism: cuts LayerNorm/residual activation memory by N_TP with zero extra bandwidth cost.

equations.title: Sequence Parallel LayerNorm Full-Hidden-Dimension Requirement & Gradient Synchronization
equations.verbatimSummary: Because LayerNorm computes mean mu_h and variance sigma_h^2 across the full hidden dimension h, it cannot be sharded along h; SP shards it along s instead. Unlike vanilla TP (where LayerNorm inputs are identical across ranks), SP ranks see disjoint sequence slices s/N_TP, requiring a tiny AllReduce on LayerNorm parameter gradients (2h elements) during backward.
equations.engineApplication: Ensures exact mathematical equivalence between TP+SP and single-GPU training.

equations.title: Context Parallelism (CP) & Blockwise Ring Attention with Online Softmax
equations.equationLatex: m_i^{(t)} = \max\!\left(m_i^{(t-1)}, \max_j S_{ij}^{(t)}\right), \quad \ell_i^{(t)} = e^{m_i^{(t-1)} - m_i^{(t)}}\ell_i^{(t-1)} + \sum_j e^{S_{ij}^{(t)} - m_i^{(t)}}, \quad O_i^{(t)} = \operatorname{diag}(\ell_i^{(t)})^{-1}\!\left(\operatorname{diag}(\ell_i^{(t-1)})e^{m_i^{(t-1)} - m_i^{(t)}}O_i^{(t-1)} + e^{S_i^{(t)} - m_i^{(t)}}V^{(t)}\right)
equations.verbatimSummary: Splits sequences of length s (e.g., 128k+ tokens) into s / N_CP chunks across N_CP GPUs throughout the entire model. In attention layers, each GPU asynchronously sends its local (K, V) chunk to rank (r+1) mod N_CP while computing blockwise attention and updating online softmax running max m_i and normalizer l_i over N_CP ring steps.
equations.engineApplication: Enables 128k+ long-context training and inference without materializing full sequence activations on any single GPU.

equations.title: Zig-Zag Ring Attention Load Balancing Under Causal Masking
equations.equationLatex: \mathcal{I}_r^{\text{ZigZag}} = \left[\frac{r \cdot s}{2 N_{\text{CP}}}, \frac{(r+1)s}{2 N_{\text{CP}}}\right) \cup \left[\frac{(2N_{\text{CP}} - 1 - r)s}{2 N_{\text{CP}}}, \frac{(2N_{\text{CP}} - r)s}{2 N_{\text{CP}}}\right), \quad W_r = \frac{s^2}{2 N_{\text{CP}}} \;\forall r
equations.verbatimSummary: Resolves the severe causal-mask compute imbalance of naive sequential Ring Attention (where rank 0 only computes 1/(2 N_CP) triangle while rank N_CP-1 computes (2 N_CP - 1)/(2 N_CP)) by assigning each rank r one symmetric early token chunk and one late token chunk, equalizing non-masked causal attention FLOPs across all N_CP ranks.
equations.engineApplication: Eliminates straggler ranks in causal long-context attention across CP process groups.

equations.title: Pipeline Parallelism (PP) Naive vs All-Forward-All-Backward (AFAB) Bubble Ratio & Activation Memory
equations.equationLatex: r_{\text{bubble}}^{\text{naive}} = \frac{(p - 1)(t_f + t_b)}{t_f + t_b} = p - 1, \quad r_{\text{bubble}}^{\text{AFAB}} = \frac{(p - 1)(t_f + t_b)}{m(t_f + t_b)} = \frac{p - 1}{m}, \quad M_{\text{act}}^{\text{AFAB}} = m \cdot M_{\text{act,stage}}
equations.verbatimSummary: Quantifies the idle pipeline bubble fraction across p pipeline stages and m micro-batches: splitting a batch into m micro-batches under AFAB reduces the bubble fraction from p-1 to (p-1)/m, but requires storing activations for all m micro-batches simultaneously until the backward phase begins.
equations.engineApplication: Establishes the fundamental bubble-vs-memory law of multi-node pipeline parallelism.

equations.title: 1F1B (One-Forward-One-Backward) Steady-State Schedule & Activation Memory Cap
equations.equationLatex: r_{\text{bubble}}^{\text{1F1B}} = \frac{p - 1}{m}, \quad N_{\text{warmup}}(r) = \min(p - r - 1, m), \quad M_{\text{act}}^{\text{1F1B}} = p \cdot M_{\text{act,stage}} \ll m \cdot M_{\text{act,stage}}
equations.verbatimSummary: Transitions each pipeline stage r after p-r-1 warmup forward micro-batches into a steady state alternating 1 forward and 1 backward micro-batch, immediately freeing activations after each backward step. Caps peak stored activations at p micro-batches instead of m, allowing large m >> p to shrink the pipeline bubble. Cross-node scaling from p=8 (1 node) to p=16 (2 nodes) drops throughput by only 14% vs 43% for cross-node TP.
equations.engineApplication: Explains why PP out-scales TP across slower inter-node interconnects (EFA/RoCE/InfiniBand).

equations.title: Interleaved Pipeline Parallelism (Looping Pipeline / Llama-3.1 Depth-First vs Breadth-First)
equations.verbatimSummary: Assigns v non-contiguous model chunks (virtual stages, e.g., odd/even layers) per GPU so micro-batches loop through the pipeline v times. Reduces stage compute duration and bubble fraction by a factor of v at the cost of v-fold increase in P2P activation transfers; tunable between depth-first (finish micro-batches early to free memory) and breadth-first (fill pipeline early) as used in Llama-3.1.
equations.engineApplication: Trades moderate P2P bandwidth for a 1/v reduction in pipeline idle bubble.

equations.title: Zero-Bubble Pipeline Parallelism (B / W Backward Split) & DeepSeek-V3 Bidirectional DualPipe
equations.equationLatex:
abla_X \mathcal{L} = (
abla_Y \mathcal{L}) W^	op \;\;(	ext{op } B), \quad 
abla_W \mathcal{L} = X^	op (
abla_Y \mathcal{L}) \;\;(	ext{op } W), \quad r_{	ext{bubble}}^{	ext{ZB-H2 / DualPipe}} 	o 0
equations.verbatimSummary: Decomposes backward matrix multiplication into input-gradient B (on the critical path for stage r-1) and weight-gradient W (only needed before the optimizer step, freely schedulable into pipeline bubbles via ILP). DeepSeek-V3 DualPipe extends B/W splitting with two bidirectional micro-batch streams from both ends of the pipeline, overlapping forward and backward compute with all-to-all MoE communication for near-zero bubble and near-zero communication overhead.
equations.engineApplication: State-of-the-art pipeline scheduling reference for MoE + multi-node LLM training.

equations.title: Mixture of Experts (MoE) & Expert Parallelism (EP) All-to-All Routing with Node-Limited Routing
equations.verbatimSummary: Distributes independent MoE feedforward experts across N_EP workers and routes token hidden states via All-to-All collectives while combining with DP for non-MoE layers. DeepSeek-V3 (256 experts) constrains router dispatch so each token is sent to at most M=4 nodes, bounding inter-node All-to-All communication.
equations.engineApplication: Governs sparse expert routing and node-locality constraints in MoE architectures.

equations.title: 5D Parallelism Composition Law & ZeRO-3 vs Pipeline Parallelism Duality Theorem
equations.equationLatex: N_{\text{GPUs}} = N_{\text{DP}} \times N_{\text{CP}} \times N_{\text{TP}} \times N_{\text{PP}}, \quad N_{\text{DP\_total}} = N_{\text{DP}} \times N_{\text{EP}} \text{ (for MoE layers)}
equations.verbatimSummary: Unifies all five orthogonal axes—DP (batch), TP+SP (hidden/seq), CP (long context seq), PP (depth layers), and EP (MoE experts)—plus ZeRO-1/2/3. Establishes the duality between ZeRO-3 (stores fractional layer, communicates weights O(h^2), prefers large b*s to hide comms) and PP (stores full layer, communicates activations O(b*s*h), prefers large GAS to hide bubble), explaining why PP + ZeRO-1/2 + intra-node TP+SP is preferred at 1,024+ GPUs.
equations.engineApplication: Master architectural taxonomy for mapping any LLM onto multi-node GPU clusters.

equations.title: 3-Step Hierarchical 5D Parallelism Configuration Solver & 4,000-Run Heatmap Optima
equations.equationLatex: \max_{(N_{\text{TP}}, N_{\text{PP}}, N_{\text{DP}}, N_{\text{CP}}, b, N_{\text{GAS}}, \text{ZeRO})} \text{MFU} \quad \text{s.t.} \quad M_{\text{peak}} \le M_{\text{HBM}}, \;\; b \cdot s \cdot N_{\text{GAS}} \cdot N_{\text{DP}} = B_{\text{target}}, \;\; N_{\text{TP}} \le 8
equations.verbatimSummary: Formulates the 3-step optimal configuration algorithm validated across 1-64 nodes of 8xH100 (s=4096, B_target=1M tokens): Step 1 Fit in memory (<=10B: TP or ZeRO-3 on 8 GPUs; 10B-100B: TP=8 + PP or TP=8 + ZeRO-3; 512+ GPUs: add PP; 1024+ GPUs: TP=8 + PP + ZeRO-2); Step 2 Hit target global batch size via DP/GAS/CP; Step 3 Maximize MFU by keeping TP<=8 intra-node NVLink and balancing micro-batch size b.
equations.engineApplication: Provides deterministic configuration rules for cluster job sizing.

equations.title: NVIDIA H100 Hopper GPU Compute & Memory Hierarchy Specification
equations.verbatimSummary: Characterizes the hierarchical execution model: 32 threads form a lock-step SIMD warp; warps form thread blocks scheduled onto 132 Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs); memory bandwidth degrades from per-thread registers to per-SM Shared Memory/L1 SRAM, cross-SM L2 cache, and 80 GB HBM global memory. Note: NCCL communication kernels consume SMs, causing compute-communication SM contention.
equations.engineApplication: Informs custom kernel block sizing and NCCL SM allocation during overlapped communication.

equations.title: Kernel Compilation Hierarchy: PyTorch Eager vs @torch.compile vs Triton JIT vs CUDA C++
equations.verbatimSummary: Demonstrates how @torch.compile captures PyTorch graphs and emits fused Triton kernels (inspectable via TORCH_LOGS="output_code"), eliminating intermediate HBM reads/writes for pointwise ops like ELU, while custom CUDA unlocks warp-level shared-memory and SM scheduling beyond block-level Triton.
equations.engineApplication: Guides kernel optimization workflow: start with @torch.compile, refine in Triton, drop to CUDA only for warp/SM-level bottlenecks.

equations.title: DRAM Burst Memory Coalescing in Row-Major Matrix Multiplication (10x Speedup)
equations.equationLatex: x = \text{blockIdx.x} \cdot B + \lfloor \text{threadIdx.x} / B \rfloor, \quad y = \text{blockIdx.y} \cdot B + (\text{threadIdx.x} \bmod B) \implies \text{Address}(B_{i,y}) = i \cdot N + y \text{ (contiguous across warp)}
equations.verbatimSummary: Proves why naive 2D thread-to-index mapping (x = blockIdx.x*blockDim.x + threadIdx.x) causes uncoalesced strided DRAM accesses on row-major matrices (adjacent threads in a warp vary x and read column elements separated by stride K). Remapping threadIdx.x mod B to column index y aligns warp threads to consecutive memory addresses, yielding a measured 10x increase in HBM throughput and 10x reduction in kernel time.
equations.engineApplication: Critical rule for all custom GPU tensor kernels: consecutive threadIdx.x within a 32-thread warp must index contiguous inner-dimension memory.

equations.title: Shared-Memory Tiled Matrix Multiplication & HBM Bandwidth Reduction
equations.equationLatex: C_{\text{tile}} = \sum_{t=0}^{K / T - 1} A_{\text{shared}}^{(t)} B_{\text{shared}}^{(t)}, \quad \text{HBM Reads Reduction} = \mathcal{O}\!\left(\frac{1}{T}\right) \implies 410\text{ GB/s},\; 6.6\text{ TFLOPS}\; (-43\%\text{ time})
equations.verbatimSummary: Cooperatively loads T x T tiles of A and B from slow HBM into fast per-SM Shared Memory once per tile step (synchronized via __syncthreads()), reusing each loaded element T times across the thread block and cutting global memory traffic by factor T.
equations.engineApplication: Foundation of block-tiled GEMM and attention kernels.

equations.title: Thread Coarsening (MIO Stall Mitigation) & Warp SIMD Control Divergence Elimination
equations.verbatimSummary: Resolves Nsight Compute MIO (Memory Input/Output) instruction queue stalls on shared memory by coarsening each thread to compute multiple output elements via wider vector loads, and eliminates SIMD warp serialization by avoiding divergent branch conditionals within 32-thread warps.
equations.engineApplication: Used when profiling custom CUDA kernels with `ncu --set full`.

equations.title: Kernel Fusion & FlashAttention-1/2/3 IO-Aware Exact Tiled Attention in SRAM
equations.equationLatex: S = Q K^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{s \times s} \text{ (never materialized in HBM)}, \quad M_{\text{HBM\_IO}}^{\text{Flash}} = \Theta\!\left(\frac{s^2 d^2}{M_{\text{SRAM}}}\right) \ll \Theta(s^2 + s d)
equations.verbatimSummary: Fuses QK^T, online softmax scaling, dropout, and PV multiplication into a single SRAM-resident tiled kernel without materializing the N x N attention matrix S or P in HBM, plus native selective activation recomputation in backward. FlashAttention-2 optimizes warp/thread-block partitioning and minimizes non-matmul FLOPs; FlashAttention-3 adds Hopper H100 asynchronous WGMMA Tensor Core and FP8 support.
equations.engineApplication: Explains how exact O(s^2) attention runs at near-peak Tensor Core FLOPS with O(s) memory.

equations.title: Floating-Point Representation Anatomy & Resolution Epsilon (FP32, FP16, BF16, FP8 E4M3, FP8 E5M2)
equations.verbatimSummary: Catalogs bit allocations (Sign, Exponent, Mantissa) and interval [1,2] resolution across 5 formats: FP32 (1/8/23, 80 orders of magnitude), FP16 (1/5/10, narrow dynamic range causing overflow/underflow), BF16 (1/8/7, full FP32 dynamic range at lower mantissa precision), FP8 E4M3 (1/4/3, 7 points in [1,2], higher precision for forward/weights), and FP8 E5M2 (1/5/2, 3 points in [1,2], wider range for gradients).
equations.engineApplication: Numerical foundation for mixed-precision and quantized inference/training.

equations.title: Three Pillars of Mixed Precision Stability: FP32 Master Weights, Dynamic Loss Scaling, FP32 Accumulators
equations.verbatimSummary: Prevents gradient underflow and weight update swamping (where |Delta w| < epsilon_BF16 * |w| rounds to zero in 16-bit) via (1) maintaining FP32 master weights for updates, (2) scaling loss by alpha_scale before backward and unscaling gradients before clipping/optimizer, and (3) accumulating reductions in FP32.
equations.engineApplication: Prevents silent weight stagnation and NaN/Inf divergence in mixed-precision training.

equations.title: FP8 Pretraining Memory & Precision Comparison (Transformer Engine, FP8-LM O3, DeepSeek-V3, Nanotron FP8)
equations.equationLatex: S_{\text{tile}}^{1\times 128}(X) = \frac{\max_{j \in [1,128]} |X_{i,j}|}{V_{\max}^{\text{E4M3}}}, \quad M_{\text{static}} = \begin{cases} 20\Psi & \text{BF16 + FP32 grad acc} \\ 16\Psi & \text{BF16 no FP32 grad acc / TE FP8} \\ 15\Psi & \text{DeepSeek-V3 FP8 (25\% save)} \\ 10\Psi & \text{Nanotron FP8 (50\% save)} \\ 9\Psi & \text{FP8-LM O3 (55\% save)} \end{cases}
equations.verbatimSummary: Compares H100 FP8 GEMM (2x theoretical FLOPS of BF16) across production schemes (Table I, p. 199): DeepSeek-V3 achieves stable large-scale FP8 pretraining via fine-grained 1x128 per-token activation tile scaling and 128x128 weight block scaling with FP32 master weights, FP32 accumulated gradients, FP8 model weights, BF16 gradients, and BF16+BF16 Adam states (15 bytes/param, 25% memory reduction). Nanotron FP8 uses BF16 master weights and FP8 optimizer states (10 bytes/param, 50% reduction).
equations.engineApplication: Directly guides FP8 quantization and tile-wise outlier normalization on Hopper/Blackwell GPUs.

equations.title: Collective Communication Primitives & Ring AllReduce Bandwidth Optimality Theorem
equations.verbatimSummary: Derives the exact per-GPU data transfer volume of Ring AllReduce across N GPUs: phase 1 (ReduceScatter) sends N-1 chunks of size Psi/N around the ring (cost (N-1)/N * Psi); phase 2 (AllGather) circulates the reduced shards (cost (N-1)/N * Psi). Proves ReduceScatter and AllGather each cost exactly half of an AllReduce (~Psi vs ~2Psi) and saturate link bandwidth independent of N.
equations.engineApplication: Fundamental collective cost model used throughout ZeRO, DP, TP, and SP communication accounting.

equations.title: Asynchronous CUDA Event Timing, PyTorch Profiler Schedules & Nsight Compute (ncu) Diagnostics
equations.verbatimSummary: Demonstrates why Python `time.time()` only measures asynchronous CPU kernel launch overhead rather than GPU execution, and provides exact protocols for `torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)`, `torch.profiler.schedule(wait=1, warmup=3, active=2)`, `ncu --set full`, and `torch.utils.cpp_extension.load`.
equations.engineApplication: Standardizes accurate GPU latency and kernel occupancy profiling across GSE ML services.

equations.title: Transformer Forward & Backward FLOPs Scaling Law (Linear 6ND + Quadratic Attention Term)
equations.equationLatex: C_{\text{fwd}} \approx 2 b s N_{\text{params}}, \quad C_{\text{bwd}} \approx 4 b s N_{\text{params}}, \quad C_{\text{fwd+bwd}}^{\text{exact}} = 6 b s N_{\text{params}} + 12 b L h s^2
equations.verbatimSummary: Establishes the canonical compute formulas: forward pass requires ~2*b*s*(16 L h^2) FLOPs, backward pass requires twice forward (~4*b*s*(16 L h^2) FLOPs for Dgrad + Wgrad), and exact forward+backward includes the quadratic attention term 12*b*L*h*s^2 (negligible when s << 8h, dominant at ultra-long context s >> 8h).
equations.engineApplication: Used to compute exact MFU and compute-to-communication overlap ratios across all sequence lengths.

equations.title: Data Parallelism (ZeRO-0) Compute-to-Communication Overlap Ratio rho_DP
equations.equationLatex: T_{\text{comm}}^{\text{DP}} = \frac{4 \cdot 16 h^2 L}{\text{BW}_{\text{AllReduce}}}, \quad T_{\text{comp}}^{\text{bwd}} = \frac{2 \cdot 2 b s \cdot 16 h^2 L}{\text{FLOPS}_{\text{GPU}}}, \quad \rho_{\text{DP}} = \frac{T_{\text{comm}}^{\text{DP}}}{T_{\text{comp}}^{\text{bwd}}} = \frac{\text{FLOPS}_{\text{GPU}}}{b \cdot s \cdot \text{BW}_{\text{AllReduce}}} < 1
equations.verbatimSummary: Derives the exact dimensionless overlap ratio rho_DP for Data Parallelism: communication is fully hidden behind backward pass computation iff rho_DP = FLOPS_GPU / (b * s * BW_AllReduce) < 1, which depends only on tokens per micro-batch (b * s) and hardware FLOPS-to-bandwidth ratio, independent of model depth L or hidden size h.
equations.engineApplication: Determines the minimum micro-batch token count (b * s) required to hide DP gradient synchronization.

equations.title: ZeRO-3 / FSDP Compute-to-Communication Overlap Ratio rho_ZeRO3
equations.equationLatex: T_{\text{comm}}^{\text{ZeRO-3,block}} = \frac{2 \cdot 16 h^2}{\text{BW}_{\text{AllGather}}}, \quad T_{\text{comp}}^{\text{fwd,block}} = \frac{2 b s \cdot 16 h^2}{\text{FLOPS}_{\text{GPU}}}, \quad \rho_{\text{ZeRO-3}} = \frac{T_{\text{comm}}^{\text{ZeRO-3,block}}}{T_{\text{comp}}^{\text{fwd,block}}} = \frac{\text{FLOPS}_{\text{GPU}}}{b \cdot s \cdot \text{BW}_{\text{AllGather}}} < 1
equations.verbatimSummary: Derives the per-block communication volume for ZeRO-3 (2*16h^2 bytes fwd AllGather + 2*16h^2 bytes bwd AllGather + 2*16h^2 bytes bwd ReduceScatter = 6*16h^2 bytes/block) and proves that prefetching layer n+1 weights hides behind layer n forward compute iff rho_ZeRO3 = FLOPS_GPU / (b * s * BW_AllGather) < 1.
equations.engineApplication: Explains why ZeRO-3 requires large token micro-batches (b * s) to avoid exposed inter-node AllGather stalls.

equations.title: Tensor Parallelism (TP+SP) Compute-to-Communication Overlap Ratio rho_TP
equations.equationLatex: V_{\text{comm}}^{\text{TP,block}} = 8 b s h \frac{N_{\text{TP}} - 1}{N_{\text{TP}}}, \quad \rho_{\text{TP}} = \frac{T_{\text{comm}}^{\text{AllGather}}}{T_{\text{comp}}^{\text{linear}}} = \frac{b s h \frac{N_{\text{TP}} - 1}{N_{\text{TP}}} / \text{BW}_{\text{AllGather}}}{8 b s h^2 / (N_{\text{TP}} \cdot \text{FLOPS}_{\text{GPU}})} = \frac{(N_{\text{TP}} - 1)\,\text{FLOPS}_{\text{GPU}}}{8 h \cdot \text{BW}_{\text{AllGather}}} < 1
equations.verbatimSummary: Derives the per-block TP+SP communication volume (8*b*s*h*(N_TP - 1)/N_TP bytes across 2 column-linear and 2 row-linear ops) and proves that overlapping AllGather with the next linear layer (8h^2 parameters) depends ONLY on hidden dimension h and TP degree N_TP—completely independent of batch size b and sequence length s!
equations.engineApplication: Crucial theorem: increasing batch size b or sequence length s NEVER helps hide TP communication; only larger hidden size h or faster NVLink bandwidth helps.

equations.title: Pipeline Parallelism (PP) P2P Compute-to-Communication Overlap Ratio rho_PP
equations.equationLatex: V_{\text{comm}}^{\text{PP,step}} = 4 \cdot N_{\text{GAS}} \cdot b s h, \quad \rho_{\text{PP}} = \frac{T_{\text{comm}}^{\text{P2P}}}{T_{\text{comp}}^{\text{stage}}} = \frac{2 b s h / \text{BW}_{\text{P2P}}}{2 b s \cdot 16 h^2 L_{\text{stage}} / \text{FLOPS}_{\text{GPU}}} = \frac{\text{FLOPS}_{\text{GPU}}}{16 h \cdot L_{\text{stage}} \cdot \text{BW}_{\text{P2P}}} < 1
equations.verbatimSummary: Derives total P2P activation/gradient transfer per micro-batch (4*b*s*h bytes across fwd+bwd) and proves that overlapping P2P transfer with the next stage compute (L_stage layers) depends ONLY on hidden size h, layers per stage L_stage, and P2P bandwidth—independent of b and s, and suppressed by 1/(16 * h * L_stage).
equations.engineApplication: Proves why PP easily overlaps inter-node communication whenever each stage holds multiple layers L_stage >= 2.

equations.title: DeepSeek-V3 Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA) & Low-Rank KV Compression
equations.equationLatex: c_t^{KV} = W^{DKV} h_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d_c}, \quad d_c \ll n_h d_h, \quad \text{KV Activation Footprint} \propto b \cdot s \cdot d_c
equations.verbatimSummary: Highlights how DeepSeek-V3 compresses attention Keys and Values into a low-rank latent vector c_t^KV before caching/checkpointing, drastically shrinking activation memory during selective recomputation and long-context training.
equations.engineApplication: Informs low-rank KV state compression in GSE long-horizon play-by-play sequence models.

equations.title: Multi-Query Attention (MQA) & Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) Parameter & KV-Bandwidth Scaling
equations.equationLatex: N_{\text{QKV}}^{\text{GQA}} = h^2 \left(1 + \frac{2 N_{\text{KV}}}{N_Q}\right), \quad V_{\text{KV\_comm}}^{\text{CP}} \propto 2 b s \cdot \frac{N_{\text{KV}}}{N_Q} h
equations.verbatimSummary: Reduces Key/Value projection parameters and Context Parallel Ring Attention KV communication volume by factor N_KV / N_Q (e.g., 8/32 = 0.25x in Llama-3 8B) while preserving multi-head query expressivity.
equations.engineApplication: Explains how GQA accelerates both Ring Attention CP communication during training and KV-cache bandwidth during inference.

equations.title: Pipeline Parallel Gradient Synchronization Gating on Final Micro-Batch Only
equations.verbatimSummary: In hybrid PP + DP training (1F1B or AFAB), DP gradient AllReduce/ReduceScatter must be suppressed on all warmup and steady-state micro-batches and triggered strictly on the final cooldown micro-batch of each stage, preventing p-fold redundant DP synchronizations.
equations.engineApplication: Prevents catastrophic AllReduce deadlocks and redundant synchronization in hybrid PP+DP schedules.

equations.title: Embedding & LM-Head Vocabulary Parallelism (Row/Column TP + SP ReduceScatter)
equations.verbatimSummary: Shards the input token embedding table (v x h) row-wise across vocabulary slices v/N_TP and exits directly into the SP region via ReduceScatter along the sequence dimension (instead of AllReduce in vanilla TP), while sharding the output LM head column-wise to compute distributed cross-entropy without materializing full (b, s, v) logits.
